reference_prolog:
/*  Self-contained SWI-Prolog program
    Jurisdiction: New York
    Focus year: 2021

    Question: In an eviction action, can a tenant rebut/raise the defense that eviction was retaliatory?
*/

% -----------------------------
% Basic jurisdiction metadata
% -----------------------------

jurisdiction_state(new_york).
focus_year(2021).

% -----------------------------
% Scenario facts (the question's factual statement encoded)
% -----------------------------

% Parties and premises
tenant(t1).
landlord(l1).
premises(p1).

% Premises characteristics (NY RPL  223-B(6) applicability)
rental_residential(p1).
owner_occupied(p1, no).
number_of_units(p1, 10).

% No statutory exceptions established (NY RPL  223-B(6))
condition_caused_by_tenant(p1, no).
tenancy_terminated_due_to_bona_fide_transfer_of_ownership(p1, no).

% There is an eviction action / summary proceeding to recover possession.
proceeding(evict1).
proceeding_kind(evict1, summary_proceeding_to_recover_possession).
proceeding_landlord(evict1, l1).
proceeding_tenant(evict1, t1).
proceeding_premises(evict1, p1).

% Tenant wishes to raise a retaliation defense in the eviction action.
tenant_seeks_to_raise_defense(t1, evict1, retaliation).

% Optional supporting facts showing protected activity + timing (NY RPL  223-B(1), (5))
protected_activity(pa1).
protected_activity_tenant(pa1, t1).
protected_activity_landlord(pa1, l1).
protected_activity_kind(pa1, good_faith_complaint_to_government_health_or_safety).
protected_activity_date(pa1, date(2021, 1, 10)).

landlord_action_date(evict1, date(2021, 6, 1)).

% Scenario helper predicate requested by the prompt:
% Succeeds when the encoded scenario statement is satisfied.
scenario_statement :-
    jurisdiction_state(new_york),
    focus_year(2021),
    tenant(t1),
    landlord(l1),
    proceeding(evict1),
    proceeding_kind(evict1, summary_proceeding_to_recover_possession),
    proceeding_landlord(evict1, l1),
    proceeding_tenant(evict1, t1),
    tenant_seeks_to_raise_defense(t1, evict1, retaliation).

% -----------------------------
% Statute translations
% -----------------------------

/* ========== NY Real Prop L  223-B (2021): Retaliation by landlord against tenant ========== */

% NY RPL  223-B(6): Applies to all rental residential premises except owner-occupied dwellings with <4 units,
% and not given effect if (a) condition was caused by tenant/household/guest or (b) termination due to bona fide transfer of ownership.
statute_rpl_223b_applicable(Premises) :-
    rental_residential(Premises),
    \+ statute_rpl_223b_owner_occupied_lt4(Premises),
    \+ statute_rpl_223b_exception_tenant_caused_condition(Premises),
    \+ statute_rpl_223b_exception_bona_fide_transfer(Premises).

statute_rpl_223b_owner_occupied_lt4(Premises) :-
    owner_occupied(Premises, yes),
    number_of_units(Premises, Units),
    integer(Units),
    Units < 4.

statute_rpl_223b_exception_tenant_caused_condition(Premises) :-
    condition_caused_by_tenant(Premises, yes).

statute_rpl_223b_exception_bona_fide_transfer(Premises) :-
    tenancy_terminated_due_to_bona_fide_transfer_of_ownership(Premises, yes).

% NY RPL  223-B(1): Protected tenant activities (modeled as kinds).
statute_rpl_223b_protected_activity_kind(good_faith_complaint_to_landlord_health_or_safety).
statute_rpl_223b_protected_activity_kind(good_faith_complaint_to_government_health_or_safety).
statute_rpl_223b_protected_activity_kind(good_faith_action_to_enforce_rights_under_lease_or_law).
statute_rpl_223b_protected_activity_kind(participation_in_tenants_organization).

statute_rpl_223b_protected_activity(Activity) :-
    protected_activity(Activity),
    protected_activity_kind(Activity, Kind),
    statute_rpl_223b_protected_activity_kind(Kind).

% NY RPL  223-B(4): In any action/proceeding to recover possession, retaliation is an affirmative defense;
% if court finds retaliation, judgment shall be entered for tenant (but tenant still owes rent otherwise due).
statute_rpl_223b_retaliation_affirmative_defense_available(Proceeding) :-
    statute_action_to_recover_possession(Proceeding),
    proceeding_premises(Proceeding, Premises),
    statute_rpl_223b_applicable(Premises).

% NY RPL  223-B(5): Rebuttable presumption of retaliation if landlord action is within one year after protected activity.
% (Effect: landlord must prove non-retaliatory motive by preponderance.)
statute_rpl_223b_rebuttable_presumption_retaliation(Proceeding) :-
    statute_action_to_recover_possession(Proceeding),
    proceeding_landlord(Proceeding, Landlord),
    proceeding_tenant(Proceeding, Tenant),
    proceeding_premises(Proceeding, Premises),
    statute_rpl_223b_applicable(Premises),
    protected_activity(Activity),
    protected_activity_landlord(Activity, Landlord),
    protected_activity_tenant(Activity, Tenant),
    statute_rpl_223b_protected_activity(Activity),
    protected_activity_date(Activity, DateA),
    landlord_action_date(Proceeding, DateL),
    within_one_year_after(DateA, DateL).

/* ========== NY Real Prop Actions L  743 (2021): Answer may contain any legal/equitable defense ========== */

% NY RPAPL  743: In a possession proceeding, respondent may answer orally or in writing;
% the answer may contain any legal or equitable defense or counterclaim.
statute_rpapl_743_allows_any_legal_or_equitable_defense(Proceeding) :-
    statute_action_to_recover_possession(Proceeding).

/* ========== NY Educ L  235-A (2021): Biodiversity research institute (not housing-related) ========== */

% Minimal encoding showing the section creates an institute and states its general purpose.
statute_educ_235a_institute_created(new_york_state_biodiversity_research_institute).
statute_educ_235a_institute_location(new_york_state_biodiversity_research_institute, new_york_state_museum_education_department).

/* ========== NY Real Prop Tax L  744 (2021): Special franchise assessment review (not housing-related) ========== */

% Minimal encoding: the section concerns court action in proceedings to review special franchise assessments.
statute_rptl_744_scope(proceeding_to_review_special_franchise_assessment).

% -----------------------------
% Helper predicates for legal reasoning
% -----------------------------

% What counts as an "action to recover possession" in this simplified model (NY RPL  223-B(4) and RPAPL  743 context).
statute_action_to_recover_possession(Proceeding) :-
    proceeding(Proceeding),
    proceeding_kind(Proceeding, summary_proceeding_to_recover_possession).

statute_action_to_recover_possession(Proceeding) :-
    proceeding(Proceeding),
    proceeding_kind(Proceeding, action_to_recover_real_property).

% Date arithmetic helpers (deterministic)
is_leap_year(Year) :-
    integer(Year),
    (  0 is Year mod 400
    ;  0 is Year mod 4,
       0 =\= Year mod 100
    ).

days_in_month(Year, 1, 31) :- integer(Year).
days_in_month(Year, 2, 29) :- is_leap_year(Year), !.
days_in_month(Year, 2, 28) :- integer(Year).
days_in_month(Year, 3, 31) :- integer(Year).
days_in_month(Year, 4, 30) :- integer(Year).
days_in_month(Year, 5, 31) :- integer(Year).
days_in_month(Year, 6, 30) :- integer(Year).
days_in_month(Year, 7, 31) :- integer(Year).
days_in_month(Year, 8, 31) :- integer(Year).
days_in_month(Year, 9, 30) :- integer(Year).
days_in_month(Year, 10, 31) :- integer(Year).
days_in_month(Year, 11, 30) :- integer(Year).
days_in_month(Year, 12, 31) :- integer(Year).

date_valid(date(Y,M,D)) :-
    integer(Y), integer(M), integer(D),
    M >= 1, M =< 12,
    days_in_month(Y, M, MaxD),
    D >= 1, D =< MaxD.

days_before_year(Year, Days) :-
    integer(Year),
    Year >= 0,
    Y1 is Year - 1,
    LeapYears is Y1 // 4 - Y1 // 100 + Y1 // 400,
    Days is Year * 365 + LeapYears.

days_before_month(Year, Month, DaysBefore) :-
    integer(Year), integer(Month),
    Month >= 1, Month =< 12,
    days_before_month_acc(Year, 1, Month, 0, DaysBefore).

days_before_month_acc(_Year, Cur, Month, Acc, Acc) :-
    Cur =:= Month, !.
days_before_month_acc(Year, Cur, Month, Acc, DaysBefore) :-
    Cur < Month,
    days_in_month(Year, Cur, Dim),
    Acc1 is Acc + Dim,
    Cur1 is Cur + 1,
    days_before_month_acc(Year, Cur1, Month, Acc1, DaysBefore).

date_ordinal(Date, Ordinal) :-
    date_valid(Date),
    Date = date(Y,M,D),
    days_before_year(Y, DY),
    days_before_month(Y, M, DM),
    Ordinal is DY + DM + (D - 1).

within_one_year_after(DateA, DateB) :-
    date_ordinal(DateA, OA),
    date_ordinal(DateB, OB),
    Diff is OB - OA,
    Diff >= 0,
    Diff =< 365.

% Core reasoning: can the tenant raise retaliation as a defense in an eviction action?
tenant_can_raise_retaliation_defense(Tenant, Proceeding) :-
    scenario_statement,
    proceeding_tenant(Proceeding, Tenant),
    statute_action_to_recover_possession(Proceeding),
    % Primary: NY RPL  223-B(4) explicitly makes retaliation an affirmative defense in such actions.
    statute_rpl_223b_retaliation_affirmative_defense_available(Proceeding),
    !.

tenant_can_raise_retaliation_defense(Tenant, Proceeding) :-
    scenario_statement,
    proceeding_tenant(Proceeding, Tenant),
    statute_action_to_recover_possession(Proceeding),
    % Backstop: RPAPL  743 allows any legal/equitable defense in the answer.
    % Retaliation is a recognized legal defense in NY via RPL  223-B, so it is within  743's scope.
    statute_rpapl_743_allows_any_legal_or_equitable_defense(Proceeding),
    statute_rpl_223b_retaliation_affirmative_defense_available(Proceeding),
    !.

% -----------------------------
% Final answer predicate (must be deterministic yes/no)
% -----------------------------

housing_answer(yes) :-
    tenant_seeks_to_raise_defense(Tenant, Proceeding, retaliation),
    tenant_can_raise_retaliation_defense(Tenant, Proceeding),
    !.
housing_answer(no) :-
    !.

% -----------------------------
% Main entrypoint (REQUIRED)
% -----------------------------

main :-
    housing_answer(Result),
    format('housing_answer(~w).~n', [Result]).


:- initialization(main, main).

expected.question: In an eviction action, can a tenant rebut/raise the defense that eviction was retaliatory?
